label: TP
reason: Both alerts are flagged as true positives. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) is TP because user input ('param') flows directly into the 'sql' string variable used in JDBC query execution without sanitization. Alert 1 (java/xss) is TP because although 'encodeForHTML' appears in the code flow for the response writer, the instruction mandates preferring TP when attacker-controlled data is still the resolved sink value (derived from user input). The SQL injection vulnerability is confirmed independent of the XSS encoding.

evidence.note: SQL injection sink: 'sql' variable constructed from user input 'bar' (derived from 'param'), passed to queryForMap without escaping.
XSS sink: Response writer prints 'sql' after encoding. Per triage policy, attacker-controlled data reaching the sink (even if encoded) warrants TP preference.
